node: Private-label co-manufacturing, specialty packaging, and value-tier consumer staples inputs
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found four US-listed direct or second-order names tied to retailer private-label/value-tier staples infrastructure: one retail supply-chain compliance platform, two physical capacity/packaging suppliers, and one staple-input asset owner with high Walmart/Sam's Club exposure. The cleanest direct node exposure is Seneca Foods for private-label packaged food capacity and Silgan for rigid consumer-goods packaging. SPS Commerce is a software/integration bottleneck around retailer-supplier compliance rather than manufacturing. Cal-Maine is included as a value-tier staple input/capacity reference because retailer service levels and private-label shell-egg supply can be structurally hard to replace, but its commodity and disease-cycle risks make the thesis less pure. Layer 1B expanded the node toward US-listed companies tied to private-label/value-tier consumer staples through scarce production capacity, retailer qualification, packaging formats, food-safety or ingredient know-how, and retailer service-level requirements. The cleanest former public pure-play, TreeHouse Foods, is now excluded from the candidate list because it completed a take-private transaction and was delisted on February 11, 2026. Remaining public-market exposure is less pure but still researchable through canned/frozen private-label capacity, cat-litter and absorbent-material private-label supply, rigid consumer packaging, and food ingredient systems used by value-tier/private-label manufacturers.
